title: Back Pew at Half Past Five
subject: a Finnish church verger who unlocks the church at half past five every winter morning, and the one stranger who always sits in the back pew for ten minutes and never speaks
caption: Nordic-style synth-folk. Warm analog synth pads, fingerpicked nylon acoustic guitar, plucked kantele on the melody, soft electronic pulse and low harmonium drone. Spacious cold-room reverb, analog warmth and slight tape wobble on the pads. Female lead, clear light mezzo-soprano, steady and clearly sung with close harmony on the chorus. Clear full voice, every word enunciated, steady sung melody on every line. 92 BPM, D minor. Hushed, patient, gently warm mood. No trap beats, no autotune, no dance drops, no distorted guitar, no big orchestral strings.
lyrics:
[Intro - fingerpicked guitar, synth pad, kantele]

[Verse 1]
Half past five and the snow's still blue
I find the right key on the ring
Turn on one lamp and the radiator
Wake the old boards with my boots

[Pre-Chorus]
Eleven degrees inside the porch
I breathe on my hands and I wait

[Chorus]
You come in with the cold on your coat
You take the back pew by the door
Ten minutes, never a word
I leave the lamp on for you

[Verse 2]
I don't know your name or your trade
Your boots are the colour of salt
Some mornings you stay for the whole bell
Some mornings you don't take your hat off

[Chorus]
You come in with the cold on your coat
You take the back pew by the door
Ten minutes, never a word
I leave the lamp on for you

[Bridge - guitar and kantele only]
Today the pew was empty
I kept the lamp on anyway

[Chorus]
You come in with the cold on your coat
I hear the door, I don't turn round
Ten minutes, never a word
I leave the lamp on for you

[Outro - synth pad, kantele, fade]
Half past five and the snow's still blue
The lamp is on
